problem: Zero-shot VLN methods built for discrete graphs (NavGPT, OpenNav) degrade sharply in continuous environments: they cannot track which sub-instruction is being executed, and text captions lose visual detail and spatial layout. Prior zero-shot VLN-CE methods also need per-step LLM calls, panoramas, or action-specific training.
motivation: Real deployment has no connectivity graph and no expert demonstrations, so zero-shot VLN-CE is the practical setting. Explicit progress tracking via sub-instruction completion criteria, plus a map that keeps visual-semantic information, should avoid the failures of text-only prompting with the full instruction.
key_idea: Decompose the instruction with an LLM into sub-instructions with checkable object/location/direction constraints, switch sub-instructions when the constraints are satisfied, and use the active constraints to build a BLIP2 value map whose superpixel-clustered regions supply waypoints.
insight: Landmark (object and location) constraints matter most, while direction constraints help only when combined with them (Table ablation 1: no constraints SR 20.0, all constraints 25.3). Selecting waypoints from a globally smoothed superpixel value map is more stable than frontier-based selection when the value changes abruptly after a constraint switch (FBE SR 21.9 vs superpixel 25.3). Historical decay and the trajectory mask together give the best SR (25.3 vs 22.3 with neither).
method: Constraint-aware Sub-instruction Manager (CSM): a GPT-4 few-shot prompt run once at episode start decomposes the instruction into a queue of sub-instructions, each with object, location and direction constraints.

Constraint satisfaction checks: Grounding DINO detects the object within 5 m; BLIP2 VQA answers 'Can you see the <location>?'; direction is computed from odometry poses over a 5-step window (cross and dot product). Min 10 / max 25 step thresholds prevent premature or stalled switching.

Constraint-aware Value Mapper (CVM): the BLIP2 cosine similarity between the RGB view and the current landmark prompt is projected onto the frustum of a SemExp-style navigable map, fused by VLFM cosine-weighted confidence averaging.
Value-map update tricks: a historical decay γ=0.5 applied when constraints switch, and a trajectory mask λ^k (λ=0.95) that discounts revisited cells to encourage exploration.
Superpixel waypoint selection: SLIC clusters the value map, the region with the highest mean value is chosen, and its geometric center is the waypoint (default size 48×48, 5 cm per pixel).
Final target and control: at the last sub-instruction, RepViT-SAM segments the target and its projected center becomes the goal; FMM plans low-level actions (forward 0.25 m, turn 30°).

setting.backbone: GPT-4 (frozen, decomposition) + BLIP2 (value/location) + Grounding DINO + RepViT-SAM; all frozen
setting.action_space: low-level MOVE FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN LEFT/RIGHT 30° / STOP, via waypoints and FMM
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE) plus a real QiZhi mobile robot

numbers_note: Real-robot results are per-instruction success counts out of 10 episodes (e.g., 8/10 for 'Go to the door'), not benchmark metrics, so they are omitted.
results: CA-Nav reaches SR 25.3 / OSR 48.0 on R2R-CE val-unseen and SR 19.0 on RxR-CE val-unseen with egocentric input, beating the zero-shot A2Nav (22.6 / 16.8), OpenNav (16.0), NavGPT-CE (16.3) and egocentric InstructNav (17.0). It is about 3x faster (0.45 s vs 1.29 s per action) and costs $0.04 vs $0.85 per episode compared to NavGPT-CE, but SPL is lower than some baselines and it is far below trained panoramic methods.
limitations: Egocentric view forces more exploration, so SPL is low (10.8) and far below trained methods.
Perception errors (Grounding DINO, BLIP2 VQA, simulator rendering) and LLM constraint-decomposition errors accumulate on long instructions; SR falls with 5 or more sub-instructions.
Constraint fulfillment is checked on only 25-trajectory human-evaluated samples, and the real-robot evaluation is small (8 instructions, 10 episodes each).
